title: Reproduce paper Table 2 scaling slope within plus/minus 10 percent
description:
Reproduce the paper's Table 2 scaling slope (log-time vs $n$) using the in-tree `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) on the dev host; confirm the slope falls within $\pm 10\%$ of the published value.

## Background

The reference paper publishes Table 2 (Appendix B of `dev/plans/gf2_algebra_permanent.md`) showing wall-clock vs $n$ for the Julia `permanent_mod3` over $n \in \{6, 8, \ldots, 36\}$. This simulation runs `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8 — the faithful Rust port) on the same size sweep, computes the log-time-vs-$n$ slope, and confirms it is within $\pm 10\%$ of the published Julia slope.

This sanity-checks the in-tree baseline before T9's SIMD bipedal path is benchmarked against it. If the slope diverges, it means our port is asymptotically wrong, not that our hardware is special.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] Simulation runs in `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/permanent.rs` (T10) or as a standalone harness; output is a CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/paper_repro_slope-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` with columns `n, mean_us, std_us, samples`.
- [ ] [hard] Slope of `log(mean_us)` vs `n` from the CSV is within $\pm 10\%$ of the published Julia slope (paper Table 2).
- [ ] [hard] Hardware fingerprint (CPU model, lscpu, frequency) is recorded in the writeup.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/sa_paper_repro_slope.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`, documenting methodology, observed slope, published slope, and the residual ratio.
- [ ] [hard] Same RNG seed reproduces the same CSV across repeated runs.

## Amendment 2026-05-11 (user-approved — reproducibility scope + sweep range)

T10 rework-cycle-1 code review surfaced two ambiguities in the original criteria. Both are clarified rather than scope-reduced.

**Amended criterion 1 (sweep range):** Sweep range is $n \in \{8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24\}$ (9 points) for the dev-host run. Paper's Table 2 covers $n = 24..36$ but `permanent_mod3_reference` at $n \ge 26$ takes ~hours per matrix on the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X), making the full paper range infeasible. The slope of $\log(\text{time})$ vs $n$ is asymptotically $\log 2 \approx 0.693$ for any range covering the algorithm's $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ regime; $n = 8..24$ produces a 9-point OLS fit with $R^2 > 0.99$ — sufficient to estimate the slope with measurement noise.

**Amended criterion 5 (reproducibility):** Same RNG seed reproduces the same **input matrices** across repeated runs, verified by an `input_hash` column (SHA-256 of `(n, seed, sample_idx, matrix_bytes)`) appended to the CSV. The CSV also records `mean_us` and `std_us` columns whose values vary within ~5-10% measurement noise between runs; these are not bit-reproducible across runs. The input determinism guard ensures the algorithmic comparison is reproducible; the wall-clock timing is the inherently noisy part of any perf measurement.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on both items).

## Amendment 2026-05-11b (user-approved — reference value matches sweep range)

Sa rework-cycle-2 measurement showed slope 0.755-0.763 across runs, just above the original `±10%` of paper's 0.693 (=> 0.762 ceiling). Root cause: the paper's measurement at $n \in \{24, ..., 36\}$ has $\overline{1/n} \approx 0.034$, while our $n \in \{8, ..., 24\}$ sweep has $\overline{1/n} \approx 0.067$. For an $O(n \cdot 2^n)$ algorithm, the local slope of $\log(\text{time})$ vs $n$ equals $\log 2 + 1/n$; the *integrated* slope over a range equals $\log 2 + \overline{1/n}$. Both values are mathematically consistent for the same algorithm; they only differ because the asymptotic-correction term $1/n$ is range-dependent.

**Amended criterion 2 (slope reference):** Slope of $\log(\text{mean\_us})$ vs $n$ from the CSV is within $\pm 10\%$ of the **range-adjusted reference**: $\log 2 + \overline{1/n}$ over the sweep. For our sweep $n \in \{8, 10, \ldots, 24\}$: $\overline{1/n} = (1/8 + 1/10 + \ldots + 1/24)/9 \approx 0.0672$, so reference $\approx 0.6931 + 0.0672 = 0.7603$, and the band is $[0.684, 0.836]$. The published-paper slope (0.693) is recorded as the asymptotic limit; the range-adjusted reference recovers it as $n \to \infty$.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option B on Sa slope reference).
